inventoryAudit.method: Unlike its DR-105 sibling, this subject has no upstream field enumerating DR-120 leftovers to compare against — G15 v7's dr120Standing is prose and v14 has no leftover-remaining list. So completeness was tested by walking v14's own structures and G15 v7's own scope statements and asking where each item lands.

Both are carried, both verbatim, both with notDecidedHere true matching source, and each is represented by an obligation — OD-P1 by OBL-ADAPTER-IMPL at leftoverDesign true, OD-P2 by OBL-OD-P2 deferred to schemas.v11 OD-1. Exhaustive against the source list.
inventoryAudit.acceptanceTestClasses: All eight carried, and each id-plus-name string equals v14's own class id and name field exactly. None missing, none invented.
inventoryAudit.atArchiveSeventeen: G15 v7's doesNot says it 'Does not author the seventeen AT-ARCHIVE-* fixture implementations'. I counted the distinct AT-ARCHIVE-* identifiers in G15 v7 and in v14's closedMap producedRidelessArchive block: seventeen, and the count is exact. They are AT-8 members, so OBL-AT-FX-AUTHORING covers them through AT-8 rather than dropping them, and the subject quotes the G15 sentence directly. Neither omitted nor double-counted.
inventoryAudit.ciAndLvClasses: The sharpest completeness probe, because G15 v7's dr120Standing says it 'consumes v14's AT/CI/LV classes' while the subject contains zero CI-* and zero LV-* identifiers. Resolved against the sources: v14's CI-1..CI-5 and LV-1..LV-4 are stated as rules, not fixture classes — hermetic-CI input pinning, networklessness, determinism, typed non-success, profile-id equality, and local-validation parity — and G15 v7's executesWhenRun places them in execution scope, 'each of the 80 fixtureMemberMap keys ... plus the CI/LV classes specified above ... Execution remains qualification.' They are therefore contract law under OBL-CONTRACT-V14 and execution under OBL-G15-EXECUTION, and their unexercisability without an adapter is already carried by OBL-ADAPTER-IMPL. Nothing is missing. A join is not obliged to enumerate every class inside its execution obligation any more than it enumerates the 80 map keys.
inventoryAudit.the51D106Fixtures: The subject says they are 'FG-3 hand-authored DR-103 admission-class evidence, not adapter-run AT fixtures.' G15 v7 says the 51 are FG-3 hand-authored evidence that the eight DR-103 admission classes exist, are not fixtureMemberMap keys, and carry no producer standing. Accurate, and it is the distinction that keeps them out of OBL-AT-FX-AUTHORING.
inventoryAudit.fixtureGeneratorProbe: Probed as a possible omitted implementation leftover, since v14's closedMap attributes 31 of the 80 map keys to a fixtureGenerator. It did not land. v14 states its standing as TEST-ONLY, not a production adapter mode, and its output is hostile DR-103 classes — so its product is DR-103 evidence, which the DR-103 join owns and this subject is forbidden to take. Its rules FG-1..FG-6 are contract law under OBL-CONTRACT-V14. Where the tool's own implementation sits between OD-P1's 'build tool' and DR-103 is a boundary no source draws; that unstated boundary is folded into advisory A1 rather than reported as an omission.

advisories.title: The inventory's scope rule is unstated, so a reader cannot tell that v14's identity dependencies were considered and excluded rather than overlooked
advisories.detail: The subject builds its DR-120 inventory from v14's namedOpenDecisions, and does so exhaustively — both OD-P1 and OD-P2 are carried verbatim and each becomes an obligation. It does not address v14's identityDependencies, of which there are at least seven, ID-DEP-P1 through ID-DEP-P7. That is defensible on its face, because those name external surfaces and ride the rows they name — schemas.v11 and DR-103, DR-111, DR-112 and DR-110, DR-102, DR-105, DR-124/106/109/113, and D-006/DR-115/DR-118 — and rides belong to the rows they ride. But the subject never says so, and it does maintain a deferredOrRidesElsewhere bucket, which it used for OD-P2. So the reader sees the machinery for cross-row deferrals used once and silently not used for a larger set, with no rule distinguishing them.
advisories.sharpestInstance: ID-DEP-P3 rides DR-112 and DR-110 and its consequence is that AT-6, AT-1-TRUSTED-INSTALL and AT-5-TRUSTED-INSTALL stay INACTIVE, which G15 v7 independently confirms in its doesNotExecute list. Three of the eight AT classes are therefore unexercisable until those rows close, regardless of the adapter or the fixture authoring. doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone tells a reader what remains leftover-design, and someone reading it as the path to DR-120 closure would not learn that.
advisories.whyItStaysAdvisory: The fact is in the artifact, not missing from it: OBL-G15-EXECUTION names all three classes and states the join does not activate them. No obligation is misclassified, nothing is closed that should be open, and there is no upstream enumeration of DR-120 leftovers that the subject contradicts — G15 v7's dr120Standing is prose and asks only that DR-120 leftover-design not be closed and no adapter be invented, both of which the subject honours. I also declined to import the DR-105 pattern here, where OBL-BLK-1..4 track cross-row blockers as leftover on the row, because there a coordinator decision expressly routed them to that row and nothing does so for DR-120.
advisories.whatWouldCloseIt: One sentence stating the scope rule — that v14's namedOpenDecisions are carried as DR-120 obligations while identityDependencies ride the rows they name — and, if the coordinator wants the ledger to be readable as a closure path, a deferredOrRidesElsewhere entry for the ID-DEP-P3 freeze on three AT classes.

Custody holds: subject 35c100d1 at 0444, 14309 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778; live required-now 26 of 26; live DR-120 token OPEN matching the artifact's own file08StatusToken; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All ten distinct cited digests reproduce with zero failures, COORD among them pinned at the live value so no append-only argument is needed, and recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head as the artifact's own clause requires. All four cited verdicts are exact: v14 Claude ACCEPT 0/0, v14 Codex ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES 0/0, G15 v7 Claude ACCEPT 0/0 with no Codex file in existence, and DR-103 join v3 Claude ACCEPT 0/0. Tracing rather than reporting showed D-108 states an explicit finding-id collision discipline — Claude ADV-1 is CLAUDE-V14-A1, Codex CPCV14-A1 / CPCV14-A2 are CODEX-V14-A1 / CODEX-V14-A2, distinct findings — and the adopted COORD entry uses the subject's three names verbatim. The subject is citing the recording it names in the same clause, and the resolving text sits inside COORD, which it pins. Refuted. On completeness, this subject differs from its DR-105 siblings in having no upstream field enumerating DR-120 leftovers to check against, so I walked v14 and G15 v7 directly. v14 names exactly two open decisions and both are carried verbatim with notDecidedHere matching, one becoming leftover-design and one routed to schemas.v11 OD-1; all eight AT classes are carried with id-and-name strings equal to source; the seventeen AT-ARCHIVE-* are exactly seventeen and sit inside OBL-AT-FX-AUTHORING through AT-8; and the 51 D-106 fixtures are correctly characterized as FG-3 DR-103 class evidence rather than adapter-run AT fixtures. The second is that live file 08 still calls the G15 harness not authored — stale, but the register's to fix, and the subject is right to refuse. One disclosure: I opened the v14 Codex verdict, reading only its verdict line, counts and advisory ids, to check a load-bearing citation the subject makes about it. It is not the other reviewer on this subject, but the Claude verdict on v14 records that its author left that same file unopened, so a coordinator reading the prohibition more strictly should discount that one verification; the three Claude-lane checks are unaffected.
